chapters.summary: 退役皇家海军陆战队少校Dexter Smythe住在牙买加北岸别墅Wavelets，沉迷喂养珊瑚礁鱼群，尤其驯养一只名叫Octopussy的章鱼。邦德以国防部名义到访，追查二战末期MOB Force在蒂罗尔Oberaurach的旧案：Smythe当年从缴获的盖世太保文件中发现藏金纸条，诱骗滑雪向导Hannes Oberhauser带路登上Wilde Kaiser，在Franziskaner Halt附近两枪将其射杀并推入冰川裂缝，盗走武器箱中两根24K金条(带1943年Reichsbank铸记)。战后他借Foo兄弟经澳门分批出售金条，每季度得1000牙买加镑，佣金10%。邦德告知Oberhauser遗体当年春天随冰川融化现身，子弹成为铁证，Smythe约一周后将被押回伦敦受军事法庭审判。邦德离去后，Smythe按原计划出海捕蝎子鱼喂章鱼，却被蝎子鱼毒刺刺中胸口，毒发约15分钟内致命；他挣扎着把鱼送到章鱼洞口，反被章鱼拖入水中溺亡。尸体被两名牙买加青年发现，当地报纸写成found drowned，邦德在档案末页同样写下found drowned并私下认定为自杀。
chapters.summary_en: Retired Royal Marines Major Dexter Smythe lives at Wavelets, a villa on Jamaica's North Shore, where he spends his days feeding the reef fish and taming an octopus he calls Octopussy. Bond arrives on behalf of the Ministry of Defence to investigate a wartime case from the last days of the war: serving with MOB Force at Oberaurach in the Tirol, Smythe found a note in captured Gestapo papers revealing two bars of 24-carat gold hidden in a weapons case near the Franziskaner Halt on the Wilde Kaiser. He lured his ski guide, Hannes Oberhauser, up the mountain, shot him twice in the base of the skull and pushed his body into a glacier crevasse, then stole the gold. After the war he sold it off piecemeal through the Foo brothers in Kingston, via Macao, receiving 1,000 Jamaican pounds a quarter at 10 per cent commission. Bond tells him that Oberhauser's body emerged from the glacier that spring and the bullets are conclusive evidence; Smythe will be taken back to London in about a week to face a court-martial. After Bond leaves, Smythe goes out as planned to spear a scorpionfish for the octopus, is stung in the chest, and dies of the poison within about fifteen minutes; struggling to deliver the fish to the octopus's hole, he is dragged under the water and drowned. His body is found by two young Jamaicans, the local paper reports him 'found drowned', and Bond writes the same verdict on the last page of the file, privately assuming suicide.
chapters.title: OCTOPUSSY

chapters.summary: M.命令邦德在柏林杀死KGB狙击手Trigger：代号272的特工在Novaya Zemlya藏匿多年后携原子与火箭情报出逃，已抵东柏林，定于连续三夜中某一夜18-19时穿越Zimmerstrasse边境；KGB已知越境时间地点，代号Operation Extase，派Trigger守在Haus der Ministerien窗口将其射杀。邦德先在Bisley的Century Range用Winchester .308试验步枪配红外狙击镜练枪至500码，随后乘午夜BEA航班赴柏林，在Station WB二号人物Paul Sender上尉安排的Kochstrasse与Wilhelmstrasse街角公寓四楼设伏，射程约300-310码。连续两夜无事，第三夜272终于现身冲刺；邦德透过狙击镜发现Trigger竟是连日所见的金发女大提琴手，其Kalashnikov冲锋枪藏于大提琴盒中，女子管弦乐队演出是为枪声作掩护。邦德在最后一刻偏移瞄准，只击碎枪支并可能伤及其左手，未取其性命，272成功越境。随后对方探照灯与枪火扫射公寓，邦德与Sender乘装甲车撤离。Sender须向站长报告邦德临阵改动瞄准，邦德承认Trigger是女人，称已吓破她的胆，她不会再做狙击手，并预计此举会令自己失去Double-O编号。
chapters.summary_en: M. orders Bond to kill the KGB sniper Trigger in Berlin: agent 272, who has been hiding in Novaya Zemlya since the war, has escaped with atomic and rocket intelligence and reached East Berlin, and is to cross the Zimmerstrasse between 6 and 7 p.m. on one of three nights. The KGB knows the time and place and has mounted Operation Extase, with Trigger waiting at a window of the Haus der Ministerien to shoot him. Bond practises at Bisley's Century Range with a Winchester .308 experimental target rifle fitted with an infrared sniperscope, out to 500 yards, then flies to Berlin on a midnight BEA flight and takes up position on the fourth floor of a flat on the corner of the Kochstrasse and Wilhelmstrasse, under Captain Paul Sender of Station WB, at a range of about 300 to 310 yards. Two nights pass uneventfully; on the third, 272 finally makes his dash, and Bond sees through the scope that Trigger is the blonde cellist he has watched for three nights, her Kalashnikov hidden in her cello case, the women's orchestra playing to cover the sound of the shot. At the last instant Bond shifts his aim, smashing the gun and possibly wounding her left hand instead of killing her, and 272 gets across. Searchlights and gunfire rake the flat as Bond and Sender leave in an armoured car. Sender must report that Bond altered his aim; Bond admits Trigger was a woman, says he has frightened her out of sniping for good, and expects the move to cost him his Double-O number.
chapters.title: THE LIVING DAYLIGHTS

chapters.summary: 6月初某日，古董珠宝权威Dr. Fanshawe向M.报告：一枚Fabergé Emerald Sphere由巴黎挂号寄给秘密情报机构通讯处职员Maria Freudenstein，申报价值10万英镑，实为失落名作，将于一周后在Sotheby's以the property of a lady名义拍卖。Maria实为已知KGB特工，三年前被招入后一直在特设隔间操作Purple Cipher，每日六次向CIA华盛顿发送由100处编造的真假混合SITREP，供苏联截获破译；她至今未领过报酬，此球即为KGB的一次性巨额酬劳。邦德推断：唯一知情者KGB驻伦敦负责人必会在拍卖会上担任抬价者(underbidder)，以把价格推高，借此可锁定其身份并驱逐出境。邦德携Wartski的Kenneth Snowman赴Sotheby's，Lot 42的Terrestrial Globe自2万英镑起拍，美国大都会博物馆方面出价至13万英镑退出后，Snowman与暗中竞价者缠斗至15.5万英镑；邦德发现后排一名摘下墨镜的矮壮男子即为暗号——戴墨镜时每次加价1万英镑，摘下即退出。MI5摄影师拍下其动作，邦德尾随确认此人进入苏联大使馆：他就是农业参赞Piotr Malinowski，KGB驻伦敦负责人，外交部可据此宣布其为不受欢迎人物。
chapters.summary_en: Early in June, Dr. Fanshawe, an authority on antique jewellery, reports to M. that a Fabergé Emerald Sphere has arrived by registered post from Paris, addressed to Maria Freudenstein, a clerk in the Communications Section, with a declared value of 100,000 pounds. It is a lost masterpiece, to be auctioned at Sotheby's in a week as 'the property of a lady'. Freudenstein is in fact a known KGB agent, planted three years earlier to operate the Purple Cipher, sending six doctored SITREPs a day to the CIA in Washington for the Russians to intercept; she has never been paid, and the Sphere is the KGB's single lavish reward. Bond reasons that the only man who knows about her, the KGB Resident Director in London, will have to attend the sale as underbidder to push the price up, and that identifying him will allow his expulsion. With Kenneth Snowman of Wartski, Bond attends the sale, where Lot 42, the Terrestrial Globe, opens at 20,000 pounds; the American (Metropolitan Museum) bidding stops at 130,000 pounds, and Snowman battles the hidden underbidder up to 155,000 pounds. Bond notices a stocky man at the back who bids 10,000 pounds at a time while wearing dark glasses and drops out by taking them off; an MI5 photographer records the gesture, and Bond follows the man by taxi to the Soviet Embassy. He is Piotr Malinowski, the Agricultural Attache - the KGB Resident Director - and the Foreign Office can now declare him persona non grata.

characters.personality_en: The text does not describe her character directly; she is efficient, and holds the gun like a professional. Bond guesses she comes from an old Prussian family or a similar family in Poland or Russia, and that her bearing is well-bred and authoritative.

characters.age_clues_en: Born in Paris in 1935, about twenty-six at the time of the story.
characters.appearance: 相貌平平，皮肤苍白略带粉刺，黑发，外表略显不洁；穿带褶边的白衬衫
characters.appearance_en: Plain-looking, with a pale, rather pimply skin, black hair and a vaguely unwashed appearance; she wears a white blouse with a frill.
characters.background: 生于巴黎，母亲为白俄流亡者，未婚生下她；母亲二战时参加抵抗运动，经营Tulip Escape Route；Maria索邦大学毕业后在英国大使馆海军武官处任翻译，因性丑闻被母亲旧友(已为NKVD工作)要挟而受控；1959年获英国国籍后经外交部推荐进入秘密情报机构，赴列宁格勒间谍学校受训，三年前被招入后一直在特设隔间为KGB工作
characters.background_en: Born in Paris; her mother was a White Russian émigrée who gave birth to her out of wedlock. Her mother was active in the Resistance during the war, running the Tulip Escape Route. After graduating from the Sorbonne, Maria worked as an interpreter in the Naval Attaché's office at the British Embassy, was compromised by an old friend of her mother's who was by then working for the NKVD, and came under Soviet control. She obtained British citizenship in 1959, was recommended to the Secret Service by the Foreign Office, trained at the espionage school in Leningrad, and three years earlier was planted to work for the KGB in a special compartment.
characters.habits: 每日六次操作Purple Cipher发送SITREP；月薪约50英镑，存于Glyn Mills银行，生活俭朴，从未领过报酬
characters.habits_en: Operates the Purple Cipher six times a day to send SITREPs; her monthly pay of about 50 pounds goes into her account at Glyn Mills, she lives frugally, and she has never taken any payment.

characters.personality: 邦德眼中为典型的丑小鸭报复社会型：孤僻、少友、因私生身份自卑，唯一乐趣是暗藏的叛国秘密带来的优越感；面对Fanshawe询问时镇定自若
characters.personality_en: In Bond's eyes a classic case of the ugly duckling's revenge on society: solitary, with few friends, nursing a grievance over her illegitimacy, whose only pleasure is the secret sense of superiority her hidden treachery gives her; when questioned by Fanshawe she is perfectly composed.

communications.description_en: In Story 1, Smythe's case would require weeks of cables via Government House and the Colonial Office to the Secret Service, Scotland Yard and the Public Prosecutor.
communications.name: 电报往来
communications.note: 第1篇：Smythe案需经总督府与殖民地部向秘密情报机构、苏格兰场与检察机关发电报往来，约需数周

communications.description_en: In Story 2, Sender uses the walkie-talkie to order the Opel Kapitan's backfires and to report to the Head of Station that 272 has crossed.
communications.name: 对讲机
communications.note: 第2篇：Sender以对讲机指挥楼下Opel Kapitan制造回火声，并向站长报告272越境成功

communications.description_en: In Story 3, Freudenstein encodes and dispatches SITREPs in the Purple Cipher to the CIA in Washington six times a day; the messages are composed by Section 100, and the Russians intercept and decipher them and treat them as genuine intelligence.
communications.name: Purple Cipher电文
communications.note: 第3篇：Freudenstein每日六次以Purple Cipher向CIA华盛顿发送100处编造的SITREP，苏联截获破译后奉为真实情报

communications.description_en: In Story 3, a man at the auction speaks by telephone to the American buyer (the Metropolitan Museum side) and relays the bidding in real time.
communications.name: 电话
communications.note: 第3篇：Sotheby's拍卖现场有专人以电话向美国买家(大都会博物馆方面)实时传价

communications.description_en: In Story 3, M. summons Bond upstairs on the red telephone to tell him about Fanshawe's case.
communications.name: 红色电话
communications.note: 第3篇：M.以红色电话召邦德上楼，交代Fanshawe的案情

equipment.description_en: Smythe's wartime sidearm in Story 1, serial number 8967362; he killed Oberhauser with two shots from it. Bond calls it a clumsy weapon and wishes for a Luger or a heavy Beretta instead.
equipment.name_zh: 韦伯利-斯科特.45左轮手枪
equipment.note: 第1篇Smythe战时配枪，编号8967362，两发子弹射杀Oberhauser；邦德称其笨重，希望换Luger或重型Beretta

equipment.description_en: Bond's sniping rifle in Story 2; the armourer replaced the single-shot action with a five-shot magazine and fitted an infrared sniperscope, and the wood and metal parts were painted dull black. Bond shot with it at Bisley out to 500 yards; in Berlin it was wrecked by a stray bullet.
equipment.name_zh: 温彻斯特.308国际试验靶枪
equipment.note: 第2篇邦德狙击步枪，军械员改装五发弹匣，配红外狙击镜，木材与金属件涂成哑黑；Bisley试射500码命中，柏林实战时被流弹击毁

equipment.description_en: Trigger's weapon in Story 2, gas-operated, 7.62 millimetre, with a thirty-round magazine, hidden in her cello case; Bond's shot smashed it and threw it out of the window.
equipment.note: 第2篇Trigger的武器，气动式，7.62毫米，30发弹匣，藏于大提琴盒中；被邦德一枪击碎并抛出窗外

equipment.description_en: Fitted above the Winchester in Story 2; at night it shows the colours of a target at 500 yards and the six-inch bull's-eye.
equipment.note: 第2篇装于Winchester步枪上方，夜间可看清500码靶面颜色与6英寸靶心

equipment.description_en: Smythe's fishing tool in Story 1, a three-pronged spear used to catch the scorpionfish for the octopus; after his death the two young Jamaicans used it to spear and kill the octopus.
equipment.note: 第1篇Smythe捕鱼工具，用以捕蝎子鱼喂章鱼；死后两名牙买加青年用其矛刺死章鱼

equipment.description_en: Smythe's diving mask in Story 1; its cork valve closes automatically less than two feet under water, which can suffocate the wearer.
equipment.note: 第1篇Smythe的潜水面罩，软木阀下沉不到两英尺即自动关闭，可致窒息

equipment.description_en: An assassination device described in a Research Station paper at the opening of Story 3: a cheap bulb-handled child's water pistol spraying cyanide gas, instantly fatal when sprayed at the face, recommended for victims aged 25 and over, with death usually recorded as heart failure. Bond thinks Freudenstein may one day be killed with it.
equipment.note: 第3篇开篇科研站论文所述暗杀工具：廉价球柄儿童水枪喷射氰化物气，喷向面部即刻致命，适用于25岁以上目标，死因多判为心脏衰竭；邦德联想Freudenstein日后可能遭此灭口

equipment.description_en: A Fabergé work of 1917 in Story 3: a sphere of about 1,300 carats of Siberian emerald, 7½ inches high, made by workmaster Henrik Wigström, with a clock movement by G. Moser concealed in the base; it sold for 155,000 pounds.
equipment.note: 第3篇Fabergé 1917年作品，约1300克拉西伯利亚绿宝石球体，高7.5英寸，工匠Henrik Wigström，内置G. Moser钟表机芯，拍出15.5万英镑

events.cause: Smythe在缴获的盖世太保文件中发现VALUTA纸条，标明Wilde Kaiser山Franziskaner Halt东100米石堆下武器箱藏两根24K金条
events.cause_en: In the captured Gestapo papers Smythe found a VALUTA note stating that two bars of 24-carat gold lay in a weapons case under a cairn 100 metres east of the Franziskaner Halt on the Wilde Kaiser.
events.effect: Smythe以逮捕为名带走Oberhauser，登山途中在冰川上方两枪射杀其颅底并推尸入冰裂缝，盗走金条并藏于树林岩石间
events.effect_en: Smythe took Oberhauser away on the pretext of arresting him, shot him twice in the base of the skull above the glacier and pushed his body into a crevasse, then stole the gold and hid it among rocks in the woods.
events.title: 盗金与谋杀Oberhauser
events.title_en: The theft of the gold and the murder of Oberhauser

events.cause: 金条难以走私出境，Smythe暂缓复员，借军情通行证重返德国慕尼黑联合审讯中心任职半年，取回金条藏于手提箱带回伦敦
events.cause_en: The gold was hard to smuggle out of the country, so Smythe put off his demobilisation, used his intelligence passes to return to Germany and work for six months at the Combined Interrogation Centre in Munich, and fetched the bars back to London in a suitcase.
events.effect: 金条藏于肯辛顿姑妈公寓地下室，婚后携妻移居牙买加，经Foo兄弟向澳门分销，每季度得1000牙买加镑，佣金10%，后被扣至900镑
events.effect_en: The bars were hidden in the basement of an aunt's flat in Kensington; after his marriage Smythe moved to Jamaica and sold the gold through the Foo brothers to Macao, receiving 1,000 Jamaican pounds a quarter at 10 per cent commission, later cut to 900 pounds.
events.title: 金条走私与分销

events.cause: Oberhauser遗体当年春天随冰川融化现身，文件与子弹锁定Smythe；邦德提及已与Foo兄弟谈话，Smythe知事已败露
events.cause_en: Oberhauser's body emerged from the glacier that spring, and the papers and the bullets identified Smythe; when Bond mentioned that he had talked to the Foo brothers, Smythe knew the game was up.
events.effect: Smythe完整供认罪行，邦德称约一周后有人押其回伦敦，案件移交皇家海军陆战队军事法庭与检察机关
events.effect_en: Smythe confessed everything; Bond told him that in about a week someone would be sent to bring him back to London, and the case would go to a Royal Marines court-martial and the Public Prosecutor.
events.title: 邦德取证与Smythe自白

events.cause: 邦德离去后Smythe按原计划出海捕蝎子鱼喂章鱼，被毒刺刺中胸口；毒发约15分钟内致命，他仍挣扎着把鱼送到章鱼洞口
events.cause_en: After Bond left, Smythe went out as planned to spear a scorpionfish to feed the octopus and was stung in the chest; the poison kills in about fifteen minutes, but he still struggled to carry the fish to the octopus's hole.
events.effect: 章鱼拖住其手臂将其拉入水中溺亡；尸体被两名牙买加青年发现，当地报纸写成found drowned，邦德在档案末页同样写下found drowned并私下认定为自杀
events.effect_en: The octopus seized his arm and dragged him under the water, where he drowned; his body was found by two young Jamaicans, the local paper reported him 'found drowned', and Bond wrote the same verdict on the last page of the file, privately assuming suicide.
events.title: Smythe被蝎子鱼毒死并葬身章鱼之口
events.title_en: Smythe is killed by the scorpionfish and the octopus

events.cause: 272的越境信使是双面间谍，KGB已知越境时间地点并布下Operation Extase，派Trigger守候射杀272
events.cause_en: 272's courier was a double agent, so the KGB knew the time and place of the crossing and mounted Operation Extase, with Trigger waiting to shoot 272.
events.effect: 邦德受命在Trigger得手前将其杀死，赴Bisley练枪后乘午夜航班赴柏林设伏
events.effect_en: Bond was ordered to kill Trigger before she could kill 272, and after practising at Bisley he flew to Berlin on a midnight flight to lie in wait.
events.title: M.下达狙杀Trigger命令
events.title_en: M. orders the killing of Trigger

events.cause: 邦德连续三夜以狙击镜观察到金发女大提琴手随女子管弦乐队进出各部大楼，第三夜枪口伸出时瞄准镜中现出其金发侧影
events.cause_en: For three nights Bond watched through the sniperscope as the blonde cellist came and went with the women's orchestra; on the third night, as the gun muzzle slid out of the window, the scope showed her fair hair in profile.
events.effect: 邦德认出Trigger就是该女子，乐队演出与大提琴盒实为枪声掩护与运枪手段
events.effect_en: Bond realised that Trigger was the girl herself, and that the orchestra's performances and the cello case were a cover for the gunfire and a means of carrying the weapon.
events.title: 发现大提琴手即Trigger
events.title_en: The cellist is revealed as Trigger

events.cause: 邦德不忍射杀心仪的女子，在开火瞬间偏移瞄准，只击碎Kalashnikov并可能伤及其左手
events.cause_en: Bond could not bring himself to kill the woman he had fallen for; at the moment of firing he moved his aim and only smashed the Kalashnikov, possibly wounding her left hand.
events.effect: 272成功越境，邦德遭对方火力扫射后乘装甲车撤离；Sender须报告其违令，邦德自认将失去Double-O编号
events.effect_en: 272 crossed successfully; Bond was raked by return fire and left in an armoured car with Sender, who must report his disobedience, and Bond expected to lose his Double-O number.
events.title: 邦德改动瞄准放生Trigger
events.title_en: Bond alters his aim and spares Trigger

events.cause: Fabergé绿宝石地球仪由巴黎挂号寄给Freudenstein，申报价值10万英镑，海关依内政部令开包检查，Fanshawe鉴定为真品
events.cause_en: A Fabergé Emerald Sphere arrived by registered post from Paris addressed to Freudenstein, with a declared value of 100,000 pounds; Customs opened it under a Home Office warrant, and Fanshawe identified it as genuine.
events.effect: M.认定此为KGB付给Freudenstein三年无酬服务的巨额报酬，证明KGB已完全相信Purple Cipher情报，可升级欺骗等级
events.effect_en: M. concluded that it was the KGB's payment for three years of unpaid service from Freudenstein, proving that the KGB wholly believed the Purple Cipher material, so the deception could be stepped up.
events.title: Emerald Sphere现身伦敦
events.title_en: The Emerald Sphere appears in London

events.cause: 邦德推断唯一知情者驻伦敦负责人必会亲赴拍卖会抬价，以防Wartski低价得手
events.cause_en: Bond reasoned that the only man who knew about Freudenstein, the Resident Director in London, would have to attend the auction in person to bid the price up, for fear Wartski might get the Sphere cheaply.
events.effect: M.批准计划，邦德携Snowman赴会，以拍卖师目光与竞价暗号锁定抬价者
events.effect_en: M. approved the plan, and Bond went to the sale with Snowman to identify the underbidder by the auctioneer's eyes and the bidding code.
events.title: 邦德设下抬价者陷阱

events.cause: 竞价至15.5万英镑时后排矮壮男子摘下墨镜示意退出，MI5摄影师拍下动作，邦德认出其为农业参赞Malinowski
events.cause_en: When the bidding reached 155,000 pounds, the stocky man at the back took off his dark glasses to signal that he was dropping out; the MI5 photographer recorded the gesture, and Bond recognised him as the Agricultural Attache, Malinowski.
events.effect: 邦德尾随其出租车进入苏联大使馆，证据齐备，外交部可宣布其为不受欢迎人物
events.effect_en: Bond followed his taxi to the Soviet Embassy, completing the evidence the Foreign Office needed to declare him persona non grata.
events.title: 锁定并跟踪Malinowski

facts.fact: Smythe为皇家海军陆战队退役少校，获OBE(军事)，时年54岁，住牙买加北岸别墅Wavelets
facts.fact_en: Smythe is a retired Royal Marines major with the O.B.E. (Military), aged 54, living at Wavelets, a villa on Jamaica's North Shore.
facts.quote: Major Dexter Smythe, O.B.E., Royal Marines (Retd.)
facts.timeline_position: 邦德到访当日，二战结束约15年后

facts.fact: Smythe有两次冠状动脉血栓，第二次在一个月前，医生将其限定为每日2盎司威士忌与10支烟
facts.fact_en: Smythe has suffered two coronary thromboses, the second only a month earlier; his doctor has limited him to two ounces of whisky and ten cigarettes a day.
facts.quote: he had had two coronary thromboses, the second only a month before

facts.fact: Smythe在MOB Force任A Force二号人物，临时中校军衔，指挥官为美军金上校
facts.fact_en: Smythe was Number Two of A Force in MOB Force, with the temporary rank of lieutenant colonel, under the American commanding officer, Colonel King.
facts.quote: Major Smythe had been Number Two of A Force

facts.fact: Smythe在Oberaurach缴获文件中发现VALUTA纸条，标明Wilde Kaiser山Franziskaner Halt东100米石堆下武器箱藏两根24K金条，随即烧毁纸条
facts.fact_en: In captured papers at Oberaurach, Smythe found a VALUTA note stating that two bars of 24-carat gold lay in a weapons case under a cairn 100 metres east of the Franziskaner Halt on the Wilde Kaiser; he burned the note at once.
facts.quote: WILDE KAISER. FRANZISKANER HALT. 100 M. ÖSTLICH STEINHÜGEL. WAFFENKISTE. ZWEI BAR 24 KT.

facts.fact: Smythe在冰川上方两英尺处开两枪射杀Oberhauser颅底，将尸体推入冰川裂缝并踢落雪檐掩盖
facts.fact_en: Above the glacier, Smythe fired two bullets into the base of Oberhauser's skull, pushed the body into a glacier crevasse and kicked the snow overhang down over it.
facts.quote: fired two bullets into the base of Hannes Oberhauser's skull

facts.fact: 两根金条带鹰徽与1943年Reichsbank铸记，Foo兄弟化验含铅10%，按89成色计价，Smythe事先已凿去铸记
facts.fact_en: The two bars bore an eagle with a swastika and the date 1943, the mint marks of the Reichsbank; the Foos' assay found them 10 per cent lead and valued them at 89 fine. Smythe had already chiselled the mint marks away.
facts.quote: the swastika in a circle below an eagle, and the date 1943

facts.fact: Smythe经Foo兄弟每季度得1000牙买加镑，佣金10%，后因打点税务每季度扣至900镑，合作持续15年
facts.fact_en: Through the Foos, Smythe received 1,000 Jamaican pounds a quarter at 10 per cent commission, later cut to 900 pounds a quarter for the cost of 'arranging' his tax affairs; the arrangement ran for fifteen years.
facts.quote: every quarter, he would visit the office of the Foos carrying an empty suitcase

facts.fact: Smythe战时配枪为Webley-Scott .45，编号8967362，邦德核对过领用与归还登记
facts.fact_en: Smythe's wartime sidearm was a regulation Webley-Scott .45, serial number 8967362; Bond checked the records of its issue and return.
facts.quote: a regulation Webley-Scott forty-five with the serial number eight-nine-six-seven-three-sixty-two

facts.fact: Mary Parnell为战时Wren，婚后随Smythe移居牙买加，两年前一次醉酒争吵后服安眠药过量身亡，自杀被掩盖
facts.fact_en: Mary Parnell was a wartime Wren who married Smythe and moved with him to Jamaica; two years before Bond's visit she died of a sleeping-pill overdose after a drunken row, and the suicide was hushed up.
facts.quote: Since the death of Mary two years before, he had loved no one

facts.fact: Oberhauser为Kitzbühel滑雪教练，灰发跛腿，战前教过十几岁的邦德滑雪，邦德视其为父亲般人物
facts.fact_en: Oberhauser was a Kitzbühel ski teacher, grey-haired and lame, who taught the teenage Bond to ski before the war; Bond regarded him as something of a father.
facts.quote: It just happened that Oberhauser was a friend of mine

facts.fact: Oberhauser遗体在当年春天冰川融化时被登山者发现，证件齐全，家人辨认，颅底子弹成为定罪关键
facts.fact_en: Oberhauser's body came out of the glacier that spring when the snows melted, found by climbers with his papers intact; his family identified him, and the bullets in the base of his skull were the conclusive evidence.
facts.quote: Oberhauser's body came out at the bottom of it earlier this year

facts.fact: Smythe被蝎子鱼毒刺刺中胸口后毒发约15分钟内致命，挣扎着把鱼送到章鱼洞口后被章鱼拖入水中溺亡
facts.fact_en: Stung in the chest by a scorpionfish, Smythe had about fifteen minutes to live; he struggled to carry the fish to the octopus's hole, and the octopus seized his arm and dragged him under the water, where he drowned.
facts.quote: You got me, you bastard! By God, you got me!

facts.fact: 邦德在档案末页写下found drowned并注明日期，私下认定Smythe之死为自杀
facts.fact_en: Bond wrote 'found drowned', with the date, on the last page of the file, privately assuming suicide.
facts.quote: privately assuming suicide, wrote the same verdict of found drowned

facts.fact: Bengry教授请Smythe验证章鱼是否会吃蝎子鱼、是否识其毒性，Smythe死前仍惦记完成该实验
facts.fact_en: Professor Bengry of the Institute had asked Smythe to find out whether an octopus would eat a scorpionfish and whether it recognised the poison; Smythe was still thinking of the experiment as he died.
facts.quote: he had promised that nice Professor Bengry at the Institute

facts.fact: 邦德以国防部名义到访，自称James Bond，Smythe认出这是秘密情报机构的委婉说法
facts.fact_en: Bond introduced himself as James Bond, from the Ministry of Defence; Smythe recognised the old euphemism for the Secret Service.
facts.quote: My name's Bond, James Bond. I'm from the Ministry of Defense.

facts.fact: 272号特工自战后藏匿于Novaya Zemlya，携原子与火箭情报及1961年新系列试验计划出逃，已抵东柏林
facts.fact_en: Agent 272 has been holed up in Novaya Zemlya since the war and is escaping with atomic and rocket intelligence and the plan for a new series of tests in 1961; he has reached East Berlin.
facts.quote: he's been holed up in Novaya Zemlya since the war

facts.fact: 272定于连续三夜中某一夜18-19时穿越Zimmerstrasse边境，其信使是双面间谍，KGB已知时间地点
facts.fact_en: 272 is to cross the Zimmerstrasse between 6 and 7 p.m. on one of the next three nights; his courier was a double agent, and the KGB knows the time and the place.
facts.quote: he'd be coming across between six and seven P.M. on one of the next three nights

facts.fact: KGB狙击手代号Trigger，行动代号Operation Extase，守在各部大楼窗口射杀272
facts.fact_en: The KGB sniper's codename is Trigger, and the operation to kill 272 is codenamed Operation Extase; Trigger is to shoot him from a window of the ministries building.
facts.quote: They plan to shoot him on the run

facts.fact: 邦德在Bisley世纪靶场用Winchester .308试验步枪配红外狙击镜练枪至500码，军械员改装五发弹匣
facts.fact_en: Bond practised at Bisley's Century Range with a Winchester .308 International Experimental Target rifle fitted with an infrared sniperscope, shooting out to 500 yards; the armourer had replaced the single-shot action with a five-shot magazine.
facts.quote: a .308-caliber International Experimental Target rifle built by Winchester

facts.fact: 邦德的任务射程不超过300码，实际狙击阵地距各部大楼黑窗约300-310码
facts.fact_en: Bond's range is not more than 300 yards; his firing position is 300 to 310 yards from the dark windows.
facts.quote: their range varies from three hundred to three hundred and ten yards

facts.fact: Paul Sender为Station WB二号人物，前威尔士卫队上尉，温切斯特毕业，牛津PPE二等，40出头
facts.fact_en: Captain Paul Sender is Number Two of Station WB, late of the Welsh Guards, a Winchester man with a second in PPE from Oxford, in his early forties.
facts.quote: Captain Paul Sender, late of the Welsh Guards, had been the obvious choice

facts.fact: Trigger实为金发女大提琴手，Kalashnikov冲锋枪藏于大提琴盒中，女子管弦乐队演出为枪声作掩护
facts.fact_en: Trigger is in fact the blonde cellist; her Kalashnikov is hidden in her cello case, and the women's orchestra's performances cover the sound of the shot.
facts.quote: She was the girl who carried the cello in that orchestra

facts.fact: Trigger的武器为Kalashnikov冲锋枪，气动式，7.62毫米，30发弹匣，KGB常用
facts.fact_en: Trigger's weapon is a Kalashnikov submachine gun, gas-operated, 7.62 millimetre, with a thirty-round magazine, a favourite with the KGB.
facts.quote: Kalashnikov, submachinegun. Gas-operated. Thirty rounds in seven sixty-two millimeter.

facts.fact: 272在第三夜成功穿越Zimmerstrasse抵达西柏林，邦德一枪击碎Trigger的枪支并将其抛出窗外，未取其性命
facts.fact_en: On the third night 272 crossed the Zimmerstrasse into West Berlin; Bond's shot smashed Trigger's gun and hurled it out of the window, without killing her.
facts.quote: He's over! He's done it! My God, he's done it!

facts.fact: 邦德承认在开火瞬间改动瞄准，称Trigger是女人，已吓破她的胆，她不会再做狙击手，并预计将失去Double-O编号
facts.fact_en: Bond admitted that he altered his aim at the last second, said Trigger was a woman and that he had scared the living daylights out of her - she would never snipe again - and expected to lose his Double-O number.
facts.quote: Scared the living daylights out of her

facts.fact: 邦德座驾为Bentley Mark IV，Mulliner改装为真正双座加大行李厢
facts.fact_en: Bond's car is a Bentley Mark IV, which he had Mulliner's convert into a real two-seater with plenty of trunk space.
facts.quote: I got Mulliner's to make it into a real two-seater with plenty of trunk space

facts.fact: Maria Freudenstein生于巴黎1935年，母亲为白俄流亡者，未婚生下她；母亲二战时参加抵抗运动，经营Tulip Escape Route
facts.fact_en: Maria Freudenstein was born in Paris in 1935; her mother was a White Russian émigrée who never married, was active in the Resistance during the war and helped run the Tulip Escape Route.
facts.quote: The girl was born in Paris in 1935
facts.quote_source: 第3篇THE PROPERTY OF A LADY

facts.fact: Freudenstein在秘密情报机构通讯处特设隔间操作Purple Cipher，每日六次向CIA华盛顿发送100处编造的真假混合SITREP，行动已运行三年
facts.fact_en: Freudenstein works the Purple Cipher in a watertight compartment of the Communications Section, encoding and dispatching lengthy SITREPs to the CIA in Washington six times a day; the operation has been running for three years.
facts.quote: Six times a day she was responsible for encoding and dispatching lengthy SITREPS
facts.quote_source: 第3篇THE PROPERTY OF A LADY
facts.timeline_position: 故事现在时往前三年至6月初某年

facts.fact: Freudenstein月薪约50英镑存于Glyn Mills银行，生活俭朴，三年任职期间从未领过报酬
facts.fact_en: Freudenstein's monthly pay of around 50 pounds goes into her account at Glyn Mills; she has lived within it and received no payment at all in three years.
facts.quote: her monthly paycheck of around fifty pounds
facts.quote_source: 第3篇THE PROPERTY OF A LADY

facts.fact: Freudenstein于1959年获英国国籍，此前在列宁格勒间谍学校受训，系经Hutchinson网络报告发现
facts.fact_en: Freudenstein obtained British citizenship in 1959; before that she was reported by the Hutchinson network at the espionage school in Leningrad.
facts.quote: she was next reported by the Hutchinson network in the Leningrad espionage school
facts.quote_source: 第3篇THE PROPERTY OF A LADY

facts.fact: Emerald Sphere为Fabergé 1917年为Freudenstein祖父设计制作的绿宝石地球仪，约1300克拉西伯利亚绿宝石，高7.5英寸，工匠Henrik Wigström，内置G. Moser钟表机芯
facts.fact_en: The Emerald Sphere is a Fabergé terrestrial globe designed in 1917 for Freudenstein's grandfather, a sphere of about 1,300 carats of Siberian emerald, 7½ inches high, made by workmaster Henrik Wigström with a clock movement by G. Moser.
facts.quote: DESIGNED IN 1917 BY CARL FABERGÉ FOR A RUSSIAN GENTLEMAN
facts.quote_source: 第3篇THE PROPERTY OF A LADY

facts.fact: Emerald Sphere由巴黎挂号寄抵英国，申报价值10万英镑，海关依内政部令开包检查，Fanshawe与Snowman均鉴定为真品
facts.fact_en: The Emerald Sphere arrived by registered post from Paris with a declared value of 100,000 pounds; it was opened under a Home Office warrant, and both Fanshawe and Snowman pronounced it genuine.
facts.quote: The declared value of the package was one hundred thousand pounds
facts.quote_source: 第3篇THE PROPERTY OF A LADY

facts.fact: Emerald Sphere在Sotheby's以15.5万英镑由Wartski拍得，美国方面出价至13万英镑后退出
facts.fact_en: The Emerald Sphere was sold at Sotheby's for 155,000 pounds to Wartski; the American bidding stopped at 130,000 pounds.
facts.quote: One hundred and fifty-five thousand pounds I am bid
facts.quote_source: 第3篇THE PROPERTY OF A LADY
facts.timeline_position: 6月20日星期二晚21时30分(原文未写年份)

facts.fact: Piotr Malinowski官衔为苏联大使馆农业参赞，实为KGB驻伦敦负责人，在拍卖会以摘下墨镜为暗号退出竞价
facts.fact_en: Piotr Malinowski's official title is Agricultural Attache at the Soviet Embassy; in fact he is the KGB Resident Director in London, and his signal at the sale was to take off his dark glasses to drop out of the bidding.
facts.quote: This was Piotr Malinowski, with the official title on the Embassy staff of Agricultural Attaché
facts.quote_source: 第3篇THE PROPERTY OF A LADY

facts.fact: Malinowski乘出租车返回肯辛顿宫花园苏联大使馆，邦德与MI5司机尾随确认，证据齐备可宣布其为不受欢迎人物
facts.fact_en: Malinowski took a taxi back to the Soviet Embassy in Kensington Palace Gardens, followed by Bond and an MI5 driver; the evidence is enough to have him declared persona non grata.
facts.quote: The leading taxi did turn in through the big iron gates
facts.quote_source: 第3篇THE PROPERTY OF A LADY

facts.fact: Kenneth Snowman为Wartski负责人，店铺位于摄政街138号，世界最大Fabergé经销商与专家
facts.fact_en: Kenneth Snowman is the head of Wartski, at 138 Regent Street, the greatest Fabergé dealers in the world.
facts.quote: the greatest Fabergé-dealers in the world
facts.quote_source: 第3篇THE PROPERTY OF A LADY

facts.fact: Fanshawe博士为古董珠宝权威，海关与CID顾问，经MI5转介至M.，凭Snowman著作中的素描认出Emerald Sphere
facts.fact_en: Dr. Fanshawe is an authority on antique jewellery, an adviser to Customs and the CID, referred to M. by MI5; he recognised the Emerald Sphere from the sketch in Snowman's book.
facts.quote: I immediately recognized the Emerald Sphere from the account and sketch
facts.quote_source: 第3篇THE PROPERTY OF A LADY

facts.fact: 邦德推断唯一知情者驻伦敦负责人必会亲赴拍卖会担任抬价者，M.据此批准设局
facts.fact_en: Bond reasoned that the only man who knew about Freudenstein, the Resident Director, would have to attend the sale in person as underbidder, and M. approved the trap.
facts.quote: you remember what this Dr. Fanshawe said about an underbidder—someone to make these Wartski merchants go to their very top price

mission_en.investigation_en: Story 1: Bond checks the captured-documents record, the circumstances of Oberhauser's disappearance and the issue and return records of the Webley, serial number 8967362, and talks to the Foo brothers beforehand to master the gold-selling chain, then uses silence and pointed hints to draw a confession from Smythe. Story 2: Bond practises at Bisley by night, then flies to Berlin and spends three nights in ambush with Sender, watching the four dark windows of the Haus der Ministerien and the movements of the women's orchestra. Story 3: Bond checks the Emerald Sphere's provenance papers, Freudenstein's personnel file and bank account, devises the underbidder trap, and goes to the auction with Snowman to identify the target by the auctioneer's eyes and the bidding code, then follows him to confirm his identity.
key_clues_en: Story 1, the VALUTA note: Wilde Kaiser, Franziskaner Halt, a cairn 100 metres to the east, a weapons case, two bars of 24-carat gold.
Story 1: Oberhauser's body emerged from the glacier that spring, and the two Webley bullets in the base of his skull are conclusive evidence.
Story 1: the Foos' assay found the gold 10 per cent lead, identifying it as wartime Reichsbank gold, valued at 89 fine.
Story 2: 272's courier was a double agent, so the KGB knew the time and place of the crossing and mounted Operation Extase.
Story 2: the four dark windows of the Haus der Ministerien stayed dark for two nights, with the muzzle of a Kalashnikov protruding from one of them.
Story 2: the women's orchestra went in and out of the building daily; the cello case hid the gun and the music covered the sound of the shot.
Story 3: the Emerald Sphere's declared value was 100,000 pounds, and its provenance papers say it was commissioned from Fabergé in 1917 by Freudenstein's grandfather.
Story 3: Freudenstein earns about 50 pounds a month and has never been paid, so the great jewel is the KGB's single payment for her services.
Story 3, the underbidder's code: with dark glasses on he raises by 10,000 pounds each time; taking them off means he has dropped out.
mission_en.objective_en: Story 1: to investigate a wartime MOB Force case from the end of the Second World War, establish whether Smythe murdered the guide Hannes Oberhauser and stole Nazi gold, and obtain his confession. Story 2: to kill the KGB sniper Trigger before 272 crosses. Story 3: to identify the KGB Resident Director in London at the auction and have him expelled.
mission_en.outcome_en: Story 1: Smythe confesses in full; Bond tells him he will be taken back to London in about a week to face a court-martial. Smythe dies the same day, stung by a scorpionfish and drowned by the octopus, and Bond writes 'found drowned' in the file. Story 2: on the third night 272 crosses successfully; Trigger's gun is smashed and her left hand possibly wounded, but she is not killed; Bond has disobeyed orders and expects to be disciplined and perhaps to lose his Double-O number. Story 3: Malinowski is identified and followed to the Soviet Embassy, giving the Foreign Office enough to declare him persona non grata; the Emerald Sphere is sold to Wartski for 155,000 pounds.

story_timeline: 第1篇OCTOPUSSY：主线为二战结束时(1945年)蒂罗尔Oberaurach行动，Smythe杀害向导Hannes Oberhauser并盗走两根金条；随后约15年间在牙买加靠Foo兄弟分批出售金条为生；妻子Mary两年前服安眠药过量去世；邦德到访当日为故事现在时，Smythe同日被蝎子鱼刺伤后葬身章鱼之口。第2篇THE LIVING DAYLIGHTS：现在时为1961年前后，272号特工携原子与火箭情报自Novaya Zemlya出逃，定于连续三夜中某一夜18-19时越境；邦德在Bisley练枪当晚乘午夜航班赴柏林，第三夜272成功越境，Trigger被击伤未死。第3篇THE PROPERTY OF A LADY：现在时为6月初某年(原文只写6月20日星期二，未写年份)，Freudenstein的Emerald Sphere于6月20日晚21时30分在Sotheby's拍卖；其背景横跨1917年Fabergé受托制作、1935年Maria生于巴黎、二战母亲参加抵抗运动、1959年Maria获英国国籍、Purple Cipher行动已运行三年。
synopsis_en:
In 'Octopussy', James Bond travels to Wavelets, a villa on Jamaica's North Shore, to confront retired Royal Marines Major Dexter Smythe about a wartime crime. In the last days of the war, serving with MOB Force in the Austrian Tirol, Smythe found a Gestapo note revealing two bars of Nazi gold hidden near the Franziskaner Halt, murdered his ski guide Hannes Oberhauser - the man who had taught the teenage Bond to ski - to keep the secret, and spent the next fifteen years living off the gold through Chinese merchants in Kingston. Confronted with the evidence, Smythe confesses in full. Left alone for a week before his escort home, he goes out to catch a scorpionfish for his pet octopus, is stung in the chest, and, dying of the poison, is dragged under the water by the octopus. Bond closes the file with the verdict 'found drowned'.

In 'The Living Daylights', M. orders Bond to kill a KGB sniper, codenamed Trigger, who is waiting in East Berlin to shoot agent 272 as he dashes across the Zimmerstrasse on one of three nights. After practising with a Winchester .308 target rifle at Bisley, Bond takes up position in a flat on the Kochstrasse and watches the dark windows of the Haus der Ministerien - and, night after night, a beautiful blonde cellist in a women's orchestra that plays in the building. On the third night, as 272 makes his run, Bond sees the cellist herself behind the Kalashnikov in the window and, at the last instant, moves his aim: he smashes her weapon instead of killing her, and 272 gets across. Bond admits what he did and expects to lose his Double-O number.

In 'The Property of a Lady', a Fabergé Emerald Sphere arrives in London by registered post from Paris, addressed to Maria Freudenstein, a known KGB agent planted inside the Secret Service to work the Purple Cipher. The jewel, worth 100,000 pounds and more, is her first payment in three years of unpaid treachery, and it is to be sold at Sotheby's as 'the property of a lady'. Bond reasons that the KGB Resident Director in London - the only man who knows about her - will have to attend the sale as underbidder to drive the price up. At the auction, Bond watches the auctioneer's eyes, spots the underbidder's signal - dark glasses on to bid, dark glasses off to drop out - and follows the man, Piotr Malinowski, the Soviet Agricultural Attache, back to the Soviet Embassy. The evidence is enough to have him declared persona non grata.
